title: Lantern and Bridge
premise: In 1913, Rafael Voss serves as driver and silent courier for Adeline Marsh, a suffragist whose letters he reads out of habit and quiet devotion. When a gaunt stranger arrives bearing handwriting from Adeline's brother Tomas—declared dead two years ago—Rafael learns that Tomas faked his death to escape a blackmail ring now entangled with the very politicians Adeline is campaigning against. The evidence implicating them must reach a ship sailing on the morning tide, past three checkpoints controlled by men who would rather the dead stay dead. Rafael, who has spent his life being invisible, must choose between loyalty to Adeline and the truth that could destroy or liberate her movement; in the end, he delivers the truth at terrible personal cost, and Adeline chooses to publish it, burning her political future to light the way for others.
about_author: Mirabel Okonkwo is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing suffragist correspondence in coastal city libraries. She writes historical fiction about the people history forgot to name.

chapters.title: The Weight of Letters
chapters.summary: Rafael Voss, POV. We meet him reading Adeline's mail by lamplight before dawn, memorizing her world through other people's words. He measures everything by what can be carried: a suitcase, a secret, a life. Emotional beat: tender loneliness disguised as professionalism.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Service Entrance
chapters.summary: Still Rafael's POV. A rain-soaked man appears at the kitchen door claiming to carry a letter from Tomas Marsh, dead these two years. The handwriting is unmistakable. Rafael hides him before Adeline returns. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into fascination.

chapters.title: What the Dead Write
chapters.summary: Adeline's POV as Rafael reluctantly reveals the letter. Her grief curdles into fury: Tomas writes that his 'death' was staged to flee blackmailers who now fund her political rivals. Emotional beat: betrayal layered over love; she needs Rafael more than ever and hates needing anyone.

chapters.title: Three Checkpoints
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. They map the route to the harbor: the police post at Millgate Bridge, the private guard at the shipping office, and the customs shed on the quay. The ship sails with the morning tide. Emotional beat: cold clarity—the planner in Rafael wakes fully.

chapters.title: The Corruption of Good Men
chapters.summary: Adeline's POV. She confronts an old ally, Councilor Bright, and watches him lie smoothly while his eyes calculate. She realizes the movement she built rests on money she never questioned. Emotional beat: disillusionment; loyalty begins to feel like complicity.

chapters.title: Invisible Man, Visible Risk
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. He rehearses the smuggling run using his delivery rounds as cover, hiding pages inside tire repair kits and coat linings. The stranger, Nils, grows reckless with fear. Emotional beat: rising tension; Rafael's invisibility becomes both weapon and cage.

chapters.title: Millgate Bridge
chapters.summary: First checkpoint. Rafael crosses the bridge with the evidence sewn into a mourning wreath for a fictional funeral, bluffing a constable who knows his face. Nils panics and nearly ruins it. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into triumph—too early.

chapters.title: The Price of Loyalty
chapters.summary: Adeline's POV. Bright's men raid the house seeking the letter; Adeline burns decoy papers and lets herself be detained overnight to buy time. She realizes Rafael may be the only person she has ever trusted completely. Emotional beat: sacrifice as declaration of faith.

chapters.title: Morning Tide
chapters.summary: Climax, Rafael's POV. At the final checkpoint, customs officers recognize Nils; Rafael creates a diversion—a lantern dropped into spilled lamp oil—and gets the packet aboard as the tide turns, but is caught and beaten while the ship pulls away carrying the truth. Emotional beat: agonizing cost, unbroken will.

chapters.title: Lantern and Bridge
chapters.summary: Resolution, alternating POVs. Adeline publishes the evidence, ending her career and freeing her conscience; Rafael, released when the scandal breaks, finds her waiting at Millgate Bridge with a lit lantern—not forgiveness, but partnership. Emotional beat: quiet, hard-won hope; visibility chosen at last.
